source.title: Three Mechanisms of Feature Learning in a Linear Network

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Reports CIFAR-10 training-accuracy outcomes that refine the claim by learning phase and initialization scale.
record.gate_note: Other training-accuracy statements concern MNIST or synthetic classification tasks, not the CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 settings in the claim versions. Figure 4 reports best training accuracy in plots without a textual outcome, so it is not extracted as a row.
record.test_reason: The ResNet18 experiment directly tests V1 in a setting with scaled random initialization: every tested scale reaches 100% CIFAR-10 training accuracy. The fully connected experiments fall outside V1's convolutional-network scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the selected empirical findings. The paper's broader conclusion is that an exact gradient-flow solution for a finite-width two-layer linear network reveals alignment, disalignment and rescaling mechanisms, with supporting nonlinear experiments. The authors explicitly limit the analytical results to data in a one-dimensional subspace.
record.recipe_differences: The CIFAR-10 experiments use a Resnet18 with scaled Kaiming initialization and a two-layer fully connected ReLU network in distinct scaling phases; they do not test the claim's full set of recipes or label conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy differs between feature learning and kernel phases in the finite-width CIFAR-10 experiment; Resnet18 test performance varies with initialization scale, while all tested scales reach 100% training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: A two-layer fully connected ReLU network with width 2000 reaches perfect CIFAR-10 training accuracy in the feature learning phase but not in the kernel phase; the kernel-phase accuracy is unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization and parameter scaling can affect whether finite-width fully connected networks achieve perfect training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The linear-network theory characterizes initialization-dependent learning times and layer alignment; nonlinear experiments also exhibit alignment and disalignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization and parameter scaling govern feature-learning mechanisms and learning times in shallow networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 9 reports departure from the kernel regime at a learning rate 15 times the reference rate, while alignment effects persist.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger learning rates can change kernel evolution while preserving layer-alignment mechanisms.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 phase comparison gives no numerical kernel-phase training accuracy in text. The Resnet18 text aggregates training accuracy across initialization scales without reporting their individual values.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 compares CIFAR-10 training accuracy across scaling regimes, but the result is shown only in a figure without a textual description of its training-accuracy values; no separate rows extracted.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, capacity thresholds, and comparisons involving smaller models, early stopping or regularized recipes.
ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and matched comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special deep-network initializations.

Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients across depth, learning-speed comparisons for those initializations, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in very deep networks.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability trajectories and divergence relative to that threshold.
Matched training-speed and learning-rate comparisons with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V1 limits_scope verdict based on R2–R3. The record also misdescribes Figure 4: its caption identifies best test accuracy and relative weight displacement, not training accuracy. Initialization-dependent generalization and alignment do not themselves test V4's signal-propagation, training-speed and depth claims.
